newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai court upholds death sentence on Iranian.
newsitem.headline: Thai court upholds death sentence on Iranian.

text.p: A Thai appeals court on Monday upheld a death sentence passed on an Iranian convicted of plotting to bomb the Israeli embassy in Bangkok three years ago, a court official said on Tuesday.
Hossein Shahriarifar, 30, was sentenced by a court last July after he was found guilty of murder, robbery, possession of explosives and attempts to sabotage.
He was arrested in southern Thailand in June 1994, after he crossed the border from Malaysia.
Shahriarifar was charged with murdering a Thai truck driver. The driver's body and a one-tonne bomb were discovered inside a truck the Iranian was driving near the Israeli embassy in March 1994.
Thai police believed the bomb was to be detonated at the embassy, but the attempt failed after the truck was involved in an accident several hundreds metres away from the embassy.
Shahriarifar, who was driving the truck, abandoned it after it hit a motorcycle and fled the scene.
He was the first foreign terrorist sentenced to death in Thailand and has thirty days to appeal his sentence at the supreme court, the court official said.
Shahriarifar was not available for comment.
